text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The British stock market ended a lacklustre note as a stronger-than-expected drop in unemployment revived inflation and interest rate worries while a key U.S. monetary policy meeting sidelined investors. The FTSE 100 share index ended at 3,926.9 down 7.4 points.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index of leading shares ended bourse trade at an all-time record closing high, continuing the rally started in Tuesday's post-bourse IBIS trade after the dollar came off lows. The 30-share DAX index closed up 39.13 points or 1.43 percent to close at 2,773.43. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,770.61.

PARIS - French stocks closed weaker with a Wall Street dip at the open accentuating the consolidation after Tuesday's year high on the Paris bourse, several bank stocks bucked the trend, however, amid revived investor interest in the sector in the wake of news that Axa and UAP plan to merge to create the world's second biggest insurer. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 11.94 points or 0.54 percent to 2,217.19.

ZURICH - Swiss share prices ended on a weaker note in slack trade and light volume as investors grew cautious given the high level of indices. "People are reluctant to act as long as the market is that high up," a dealer said, adding a futures correction may trigger a year-end rally. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 1.75 points to 2,443.97.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks finished lamely, shedding all of their gains accumulated on Tuesday, brokers said, they added the market was battered by profit-taking as well as intermittent selling bouts of futures, with the market direction unclear and domestic investors quiet. At the end of the day, the Nikkei 225 average had lost 226.99 points or 1.07 percent ending at 20,979.44.

HONG KONG - A surge in property stocks led Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index to a record close, with investors encouraged by the outlook for both interest rates and the property market.The index closed up 137.38 points to 12,943.69.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended a subdued session slightly firmer, the continuing decline of News Corp since its first quarter results on Tuesday holding back the market which nervously eyed a buoyant Wall Street. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 3.4 points higher at 2,346.9.

JOHANNESBURG - Caution was the watchword on the South African stock market, as shares clung to weaker levels after earlier being knocked down by futures trading, dealers said players were nervous of being caught offsides by futures arbitreurs, who have been blamed for the volatile dealings on the bourse this week. At the close the industrial index was 16.1 points weaker at 7,914.1 pushing the overall index down to 6,755.3, off 7.3 points on the day and the gold index finished up 10.3 points at 1,711.9.
